chunks: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi informed me, saying: Abu Talib Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Bahlool narrated to us, saying: Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Dhareer narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Arqam narrated to me, saying: Abu Harun al-Abdi narrated to me, from Abu Aqeel, who said:

We were in the presence of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah's blessings be upon him, when he said: "This Ummah will surely divide into seventy-three sects. And by the One in whose Hand is my soul, all the sects will have gone astray, except those who followed me and were among my Shia."

key_terms.شيعتي: My Shia, my partisans/followers — those who support and follow Ali and his descendants
key_terms.ضالة: Astray, misguided, deviated from the true path
key_terms.فرقة: Sect, faction, group that has split off

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the seventy-three sects of Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, in the presence of his companions, prophesied that the Muslim Ummah would split into seventy-three sects, echoing a well-known prophetic tradition. He then added his own authoritative declaration that all sects would be misguided except those who follow him and are counted among his Shia (partisans). This statement reflects the Shia creedal position on the necessity of following the Imam after the Prophet.
